title: Geo-aware Incident Evidence Orchestration & Entitlement Quarantine Playbook
author: Sophia Ramirez
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a coordinated response for incidents that implicate cross-border data residency, high-privilege entitlement changes, or suspected authorization forensics. It combines RBAC-driven entitlement quarantine steps with audit-log evidence orchestration so that legal, security, and engineering teams can preserve required artifacts for compliance and investigation while minimizing impact to customers.

Context and rationale:
- Redwood operates multi-region model serving and private deployments. Incidents that cross jurisdictional boundaries increase legal complexity and evidence requirements.
- Standard incident playbooks address containment and mitigation but often lack a structured evidence packaging workflow that respects data residency and chain-of-custody constraints.
- This document codifies: (1) how to quarantine entitlements safely, (2) what audit sources to collect (and how to tag them), and (3) how to package artifacts for cross-team handoffs and regulatory audits.

Scope:
- Applies to incidents with any of the following characteristics: unauthorized privilege escalation, suspected data exfiltration involving model inputs/outputs, cross-region data access that may trigger legal hold, or incidents requiring regulatory evidence.
- Out of scope: routine account lockouts, low-severity auth failures without access to sensitive data.

Roles & ownership:
- Incident Commander (IC): Security on-call (primary) — coordinates runbook steps and evidence handoff.
- Entitlement Owner: Identity & Access Management (IAM) team — executes RBAC quarantine actions.
- Forensics Lead: Security Research / Security Engineering — collects and packages telemetry.
- Legal / Compliance: Legal counsel — provides guidance on cross-border hold and evidence disclosure.
- Engineering responders: service owners for impacted services — implement mitigations and preserve service artifacts.

Prerequisites & access:
- Access to audit event store (ElasticSearch/Kibana, or Splunk/SIEM) with read-export privileges.
- Export bucket for evidence (S3 with restricted policy; retention tag applied).
- Service account for packaging that supports temporary just-in-time (JIT) elevation and is logged (do not use personal accounts).

When to invoke this playbook (trigger examples):
1) Alert: anomalous entitlement binding to a high-privilege role (e.g., service-admin) detected across two regions within 5 minutes.
2) Report: customer or partner reports suspected model-input exfiltration where data residency might be implicated.
3) Audit: automated policy detects cross-account access to PII-labeled inference payloads.

High-level workflow (summary):
1) Triage & risk classification (IC) — decide containment vs. full evidence orchestration.
2) Safe quarantine of entitlements (IAM) — apply temporary deny bindings and flag changes.
3) Evidence collection (Forensics Lead) — snapshot RBAC logs, access tokens, model traffic traces, and system telemetry with region tags.
4) Packaging & chain-of-custody (Forensics Lead + Legal) — create signed manifest, store artifacts in restricted S3 path, and log every action.
5) Handoff & retention (IC + Legal) — finalize retention policy and notify stakeholders.

Detailed runbook: step-by-step
1) Triage & scope (IC — first 10 minutes)
   - Confirm alert legitimacy (match alert id to event stream).
   - Classify severity: P0 (probable data exfiltration), P1 (high-privilege change), P2 (suspicious but contained).
   - If P0 or P1, mark incident as "evidence-orchestration required" and notify Legal.

2) Preventative entitlement quarantine (IAM — 10–30 minutes)
   - Create a temporary deny binding for the affected role(s) using policy path /quarantine/auto.
   - Example CLI to add deny binding (GCP-style pseudo):
       rbacctl deny --role service-admin --target-principal "svc-account:impacted" --expires-in 48h --reason "incident-quarantine-<INC_ID>"
   - If platform supports feature flags, place affected endpoints into read-only or degraded mode instead of full deny to preserve customer experience when appropriate.
   - Record the change: log an audit entry in the entitlement-change index with fields: inc_id, actor, pre_state_hash, post_state_hash, reason.

3) Evidence collection (Forensics Lead — 30–90 minutes)
   - Required sources (collect as full exports, do not redact):
     * RBAC decision logs (authz_decisions) including token hashes, TTLs, and policy version.
     * Admission and API gateway logs for the affected time window (±1 hour by default).
     * Model input/output streams where available (ingress/egress) with region tag.
     * System-level telemetry (process dumps, kernel logs) if service compromise suspected.
     * Configuration snapshots (IAM policy versions, feature flag states, rollout metadata).
   - Tag every artifact with metadata: inc_id, region, data_sensitivity (PII/PHI/None), legal_hold_flag, collected_by.
   - Example SIEM query (Elasticsearch DSL) to retrieve authz decisions for a principal:
       {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"term": {"principal_id": "svc-account:impacted"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-1h", "lte": "now+1h"}}}]}}}
   - Export commands: prefer raw JSONL exports; gzip and compute SHA256 for each file.

4) Evidence packaging & chain-of-custody (Forensics Lead + Legal — 90–180 minutes)
   - Canonical storage path: s3://evidence-redwood/<inc-year>/<inc-id>/<region>/<artifact-type>/<sha256>.gz
   - Manifest template (CSV/JSON) with columns (manifest_id, inc_id, artifact_path, sha256, collected_at_utc, collector, access_policy_id).
   - Sign manifest with forensics signing key and store signature alongside manifest.
   - Chain-of-custody log must include every action (who accessed, why, what files, and any transfers).

5) Controlled access & legal hold (Legal + IC — ongoing)
   - Legal applies legal_hold=true to the manifest and sets retention policy (N days) in evidence DB.
   - Only named reviewers and forensics staff may request decryption/preview. All requests must be documented in the chain-of-custody.

6) Recovery & rollback (Engineering responders — as needed)
   - After containment and evidence freeze, rollout validated fixes or credential rotations.
   - Revert quarantine policies only when IC approves and when re-test shows no residual risk.

Artifact manifest (example table represented as text):
- artifact_path: s3://evidence-redwood/2026/INC-12345/us-west-2/authz_decisions.jsonl.gz
- sha256: 2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c...
- collected_at_utc: 2026-02-28T14:32:21Z
- collector: svc-forensics-1
- data_sensitivity: PII
- legal_hold: true

Retention, export, and disclosure rules:
- Default evidence retention: 365 days from incident close, unless legal_hold extends it.
- Cross-border exports: do not export artifacts from a region A to investigators in region B without Legal approval. Instead, Legal will advise: (a) obtain consent, (b) execute DPA amendment, or (c) perform in-region review by a cleared reviewer.

SLOs and telemetry to track playbook effectiveness:
- Time to quarantine entitlements: target < 30 minutes (metric: median over last 90 days).
- Time to initial evidence snapshot: target < 90 minutes for P0/P1 incidents.
- Packaging completeness rate: % incidents with full manifest and signatures (target > 98%).

Search snippets & helpful queries (examples)
- Kibana filter for cross-region accesses: principal:svc-account* AND event_type:authz_decision AND tags.region:
- Sample KQL to find rapid entitlement bindings: (event_type:policy_change AND fields.role:service-admin) | stats count by actor, role, region | where count > 3

Post-incident activities (within 7 days):
1) Forensics report (Forensics Lead) — include timeline, artifacts list, proof of quarantine, root-cause hypothesis, recommended mitigations.
2) Legal evidence review — document any compelled disclosures, jurisdictional constraints, and retention adjustments.
3) Post-incident review (IC + stakeholders) — update RBAC and audit logging policies; add automation to close observed gaps.

Tooling & automation recommendations:
- Add an "inc_id" header to all entitlement-change audit events to simplify grouping.
- Automate temporary deny binding rollback with a safe-expiry and audit-only dry-run mode.
- Provide a templated evidence S3 bucket with applied KMS keys and access policies for forensics teams.

Appendix A — Example manifest JSON (single-line for readability):
{"manifest_id": "m-2026-INC-12345", "inc_id": "INC-12345", "entries": [{"artifact_path": "s3://evidence-redwood/2026/INC-12345/us-west-2/authz_decisions.jsonl.gz", "sha256": "2b7e15...", "collected_at_utc": "2026-02-28T14:32:21Z", "collector": "svc-forensics-1"}], "signed_by": "forensics-signing-key-v2"}

Appendix B — Communication checklist when invoking cross-border evidence orchestration:
- Notify Legal within first 10 minutes.
- Notify Privacy Officer if PII may be involved.
- Create an "evidence-orchestration" channel and invite IAM, Forensics, Legal, and the service owner.
- Start chain-of-custody ledger immediately.
